The change applies to deletions accepted at or after 2028-06-18T00:00:00Z. A deletion accepted before that instant keeps its original 48-hour window; it receives no retroactive extension. The acceptance timestamp recorded by the service, not the time a user clicks Delete, determines the applicable policy and starts the window. Restore is allowed only while the service time is strictly earlier than recover_until. At exactly recover_until the archive is no longer restorable. Deletion details display both deleted_at, the service acceptance timestamp, and recover_until, the authoritative restore deadline. These timestamps are displayed in UTC. The Trash view in the workspace console lists recoverable archives. A Workspace Administrator can use the Restore action in Trash. Successful restoration returns the archive to the same workspace with its prior archive ID. The existing permanent-delete action bypasses the recovery window and cannot be undone. The recovery-window change does not change live archive retention. No workspace setting or administrator opt-in is required. An archive whose ordinary deletion was accepted at 2028-06-17T23:50:00Z has a recovery deadline of 2028-06-19T23:50:00Z. An archive whose ordinary deletion was accepted at 2028-06-18T00:10:00Z has a recovery deadline of 2028-06-21T00:10:00Z. Thus old-policy and new-policy deleted archives can coexist after the effective instant. Administrators should use the displayed recover_until value for a specific archive instead of calculating a deadline from the current calendar date or a local click time. # Deleted archive recovery now lasts 72 hours

## Summary

Packet Archive now provides a 72-hour recovery window for ordinary archive deletions accepted at or after **2028-06-18T00:00:00Z**. Deletions accepted before that instant keep their original 48-hour window. The change is automatic and requires no workspace setting or administrator opt-in.

This update affects how long a deleted archive remains recoverable. It does not change live archive retention or the existing console workflow for restoring an archive.

## Which window applies

The service's deletion acceptance timestamp determines the policy. That timestamp also starts the recovery window. The time you click Delete is not the policy boundary: a click just before the effective instant can still produce a 72-hour window if the service accepts the deletion at or after that instant.

| Deletion accepted by the service | Recovery window |
| --- | --- |
| Before 2028-06-18T00:00:00Z | 48 hours from acceptance. |
| At or after 2028-06-18T00:00:00Z | 72 hours from acceptance. |

Earlier deletions receive no retroactive extension. Both policy groups can therefore appear among deleted archives after the change takes effect. Use the deadline recorded for the individual archive rather than assuming every entry now has three days available.

## Read the recorded deadline

Deletion details show two UTC timestamps:

- `deleted_at` is the service acceptance timestamp.
- `recover_until` is the authoritative restore deadline.

Restoration is allowed only while service time is strictly earlier than `recover_until`. At exactly `recover_until`, the archive is no longer restorable. Plan recovery against that displayed deadline rather than a local click time or the current calendar date.

These examples show the boundary in practice:

| Accepted deletion | Recorded recovery deadline | Explanation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2028-06-17T23:50:00Z | 2028-06-19T23:50:00Z | Accepted before the change; the 48-hour window remains. |
| 2028-06-18T00:10:00Z | 2028-06-21T00:10:00Z | Accepted after the change; the 72-hour window applies. |

The first archive does not acquire a later deadline when the new policy starts. The second archive receives its longer window from its own acceptance time, not from midnight on the effective date.

## Restore through the existing workflow

In the workspace console, open **Trash** to view recoverable archives. A **Workspace Administrator** can select an archive and use **Restore** while its recovery window remains open. Successful restoration returns the archive to the same workspace with its prior archive ID.

Check `recover_until` for the archive you intend to restore before acting. The longer default window does not remove the per-archive deadline, and older deletions can still have the shorter window. The timestamp in deletion details is the practical reference for both groups.

## Scope of the change

The existing permanent-delete action still bypasses the recovery window and cannot be undone. A 72-hour recovery period applies to eligible ordinary deletions, not to permanent deletion.

Live archive retention is unchanged. Administrators do not need to reconfigure workspaces or enroll in the new policy; service acceptance at the effective boundary determines which window an ordinary deletion receives.
